plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A cormous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped lilac-pink flowers in autumn with no leaves present. The strap-like foliage emerges the following spring and dies back by summer. All parts are highly toxic.
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges in Europe and North Africa; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the natural source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout and used by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall rhizomatous perennial that forms dense colonies topped with arching plumes of tiny golden-yellow flower heads. It is a major late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other insects.
plants.location: Prairies, roadsides, and fields across North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often wrongly blamed for hay fever; the real culprit is usually ragweed, whose wind-borne pollen blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: A robust perennial with hairy stems and masses of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It thrives in moist meadows and is a critical food source for migrating monarch butterflies.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America in meadows, wet prairies, and roadsides; popular in cultivated gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The flower heads close at night and on cloudy days, reopening when sunlight returns.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A deciduous tree that covers itself in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers before the new leaves emerge. In the Southern Hemisphere, spring bloom begins around this time and carpets streets with fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late spring in the Southern Hemisphere (September to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina, and warm regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Pretoria in South Africa is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of the tens of thousands of these trees lining its streets.
